Rashi on Chullin 70b:10:1.english: Rather, what is this - [That is, what is the] carcass where there is a distinction between the carcass of a non-kosher [animal] and [that of] a kosher [animal]:

Rashi on Chullin 70b:10:2.hebrew: זו נבלת עובר - דהא בנולדה ליכא לאוקמה, דהא נבלת טהורה מטמאה, דכתיב: "[וכי] ימות מן הבהמה אשר היא לכם וגו'"; אלא בנבלת עובר מיתוקמא, שבטהור' טהור מקל וחומר, ובטמאה טמא, דליכא קל וחומר, דקם ליה ממילא בטומאת נבלות מאחר שמת, ולא דרשי' היקשא:
Rashi on Chullin 70b:10:2.english: This is the carcass of a fetus - For it cannot be established [as referring] to a born [animal], since the carcass of a kosher [animal] imparts impurity, as it is written: "[And if] an animal of which you [may eat] dies, etc." [Leviticus 11:39]; rather, it is established [as referring] to the carcass of a fetus, for [a fetus] in a kosher [animal] is pure by an a fortiori argument, whereas [one] in a non-kosher [animal] is impure, for there is no a fortiori argument, as it remains automatically in [a state of] carcass impurity once it has died, and we do not expound the juxtaposition:

Rashi on Chullin 70b:11:1.hebrew: אי לאו דר' יצחק הוה אמינא כוליה האי קרא לכדרבי אתא - דאמרי' לקמן (חולין דף עא.) אקרא, אני חיה בהמה למה נאמרה כו', ועובר טמאה דטהור תיפוק לן מהקישא דלעיל; ואע"ג דרבי מבהמה טמאה נפקא, ודרב נחמן תיפוק מחיה, הא קיימא לן (שבועות דף יט.): פרשה שנאמרה ונשנית, מפני חידוש אחד נשנית. השתא דכתיב "כל הולך על כפיו", דאפקנא מהיקשא דלא נקיט, דרשי' מ"בנבלת חיה טמאה", ואמרינן לדרשה אתא לאתויי עובר:
Rashi on Chullin 70b:11:1.english: Were it not for [the derivation of] Rabbi Yitzchak, I would say that this entire verse comes [to teach] that which Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi derived] - as we say later (Chullin 71a) regarding the verse, "[I...] why is *chayah* [and] *behemah* stated, etc.?", and [as for] a fetus of a non-kosher [animal], that it is pure, [it would be derived] for us from the *hekesh* [scriptural analogy] above. And even though Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi's teaching] is derived from *behemah teme'ah* [a non-kosher domesticated animal], and Rav Nachman's [teaching] could be derived from *chayah* [an undomesticated animal], behold, we hold (Shevuot 19a): a passage that was stated and repeated was repeated [only] for the sake of one new [teaching]. Now that it is written, "Whatever walks on its paws" [Leviticus 11:27], which removed it from the *hekesh* so that it does not hold [that comparison], we expound from "the carcass of a non-kosher undomesticated animal" [Leviticus 5:2], and we say it comes for an exposition, to include a fetus:

Rashi on Chullin 70b:12:1.hebrew: הכי גרסי' תניא אמר ר' יונתן נמתי לו לבן עזאי - "נמתי" — אמרתי. "למדנו כו'" — דכתיב: "או בנבלת חיה טמאה או בנבלת בהמה טמאה", וכתיב: "וכי ימות מן הבהמה אשר היא לכם לאכלה". הרי חיה טמאה ובהמה טמאה ובהמה טהורה, אבל נבלת חיה טהורה לא למדנו שתטמא, ומנין:
Rashi on Chullin 70b:12:1.english: This is the reading: "It was taught [in a baraita]: Rabbi Yonatan said, 'I said [namti] to ben Azzai'" - "Namti" [means] "I said." "We have learned, etc." — as it is written: "or the carcass of a non-kosher undomesticated animal, or the carcass of a non-kosher domesticated animal" [Leviticus 5:2], and it is written: "And if a domesticated animal dies, of those that are yours to eat" [Leviticus 11:39]. Thus, [we have learned the impurity of] a non-kosher undomesticated animal, a non-kosher domesticated animal, and a kosher domesticated animal; however, we have not learned that the carcass of a kosher undomesticated animal imparts impurity — so from where [is it derived]:

Rashi on Chullin 70b:13:1.hebrew: בכל החיה - להביא חיה טהורה, וכתיב בסיפיה: "הנוגע בנבלתם יטמא":
Rashi on Chullin 70b:13:1.english: Among any undomesticated animal - [This comes] to include a kosher undomesticated animal, and it is written at the end of [the verse]: "Whoever touches their carcass shall become impure."

Rashi on Chullin 70b:14:1.hebrew: למהלכי כפים בחיה - עובר טמא במעי אמו, כדאמרן:
Rashi on Chullin 70b:14:1.english: [That] walk on [their] paws inside an undomesticated animal - [This refers to] an impure fetus in its mother's womb, as we said [earlier].

Rashi on Chullin 70b:15:1.hebrew: נמתי לו וכי ימות מן הבהמה וגו' - וכיון דפרט לך בהמה טהורה וטמאה, הרי חיה טהורה בכלל, לפי שלמדנו במקום אחר "חיה בכלל בהמה ובהמה בכלל חיה" כדאמרינן לקמן. ומעתה תהא לך חיה טהורה בכלל בהמה טהורה, אם תצטרך ללמוד חיה טהורה מבהמה טהורה כלום:
Rashi on Chullin 70b:15:1.english: I said to him, "And when a domesticated animal dies," etc. - And since [Scripture] specified for you a kosher and a non-kosher domesticated animal [behema], a kosher undomesticated animal [ḥayya] is included, since we learned elsewhere [that] "a ḥayya is included in [the category of] a behema, and a behema is included in [the category of] a ḥayya," as we say later [in the Gemara]. And from now on, a kosher ḥayya will be included for you in [the category of] a kosher behema, should you need to derive anything [concerning] a kosher ḥayya from a kosher behema:

Rashi on Chullin 70b:16:1.hebrew: וחיה טמאה בכלל בהמה טמאה - לכשתצטרך. ולקמן מפרש למאי הלכתא. וסידרה ה"ג: ולמדנו חיה בכלל בהמה, ובהמה בכלל חיה, חיה טהורה בכלל בהמה טהורה, חיה טמאה בכלל בהמה טמאה, בהמה טמאה בכלל חיה טמאה, בהמה טהורה בכלל חיה טהורה:
Rashi on Chullin 70b:16:1.english: And a non-kosher chayah is included in a non-kosher behemah - when it is needed; and later [the Gemara] explains for what halakhah [this applies]. And its order [of clauses] is read thus: "And we learned: a chayah is included in a behemah, and a behemah is included in a chayah; a kosher chayah is included in a kosher behemah, a non-kosher chayah is included in a non-kosher behemah, a non-kosher behemah is included in a non-kosher chayah, [and] a kosher behemah is included in a kosher chayah":

Rashi on Chullin 70b:1:1.english: The shepherd reached his hand - into its womb:

Rashi on Chullin 70b:1:2.english: Pure - The reason for both of them is explained in the Gemara:

Rashi on Chullin 70b:2:1.hebrew: ק"ו - כלומר, אפי' לר' עקיבא דאמר לקמן (חולין דף עב.) טומאה בלועה, כגון עובר במעי אשה, טמאה — הכא מודה מק"ו: אם הועילה לו מחיצת אמו להתירו באכילה בשחיטתה אע"פ שהוא מת, לא תועיל לו כשהיא חיה לטהרו מלטמא:
Rashi on Chullin 70b:2:1.english: An a fortiori inference [kal vachomer] - That is to say, even according to Rabbi Akiva, who says later (Chullin 72a) [that] swallowed impurity — such as a fetus in a woman's womb — is impure, here he concedes based on an a fortiori inference: if the partition of its mother was effective for it to permit it for consumption through her slaughter even though it is dead, should it not be effective for it while she is alive to render it pure from imparting impurity:

Rashi on Chullin 70b:3:1.hebrew: איתקש - נבלת טמאה לנבלת טהורה, מי שאינו קרוי נבלה בטהורה אינו קרוי בטמאה:
Rashi on Chullin 70b:3:1.english: [It] is juxtaposed - [that is,] the carcass of a non-kosher [animal] to the carcass of a kosher [animal]: whatever is not called a carcass in [the case of] a kosher [animal] is not called [a carcass] in [the case of] a non-kosher [animal]:

Rashi on Chullin 70b:4:1.english: On its paws - [an animal] whose hooves are not split:

Rashi on Chullin 70b:4:2.hebrew: מהלכי כפים בחיה - בתוך גופה של בהמה חיה, דהיינו עובר טמא במעי אמו:
Rashi on Chullin 70b:4:2.english: [Those] that walk on [their] paws in an animal - [meaning] inside the body of a living animal, that is, an impure fetus in its mother's womb:

Rashi on Chullin 70b:4:3.hebrew: טמאתי לך - משום נבלה, דכתיב בסיפיה: "הנוגע בנבלתם יטמא":
Rashi on Chullin 70b:4:3.english: I rendered [them] impure for you - [That is,] as a carcass, as it is written at the end of [the verse]: "Whoever touches their carcass shall become impure":

Rashi on Chullin 70b:5:2.english: Inside a cow, [it] should become impure - For it is [an animal that] walks on paws:

Rashi on Chullin 70b:5:3.hebrew: ומשני מהלכי כפים במהלכי ארבע - בעינן, דהכי כתיב: "הולך על כפיו בכל החיה ההולכת על ארבע", שאין לאמו אלא ד' רגלים, כגון טמאה שאין פרסותיה סדוקות:
Rashi on Chullin 70b:5:3.english: And [the Gemara] answers: [An animal that] walks on paws inside [an animal that] walks on four - [is what] we require, for thus it is written: "that walks on its paws, among all the animals that walk on four," [meaning] that its mother has only four legs, such as an impure [animal] whose hooves are not split:

Rashi on Chullin 70b:6:1.hebrew: פרה במעי גמל - בהמה טמאה שעוברה מין טהור:
Rashi on Chullin 70b:6:1.english: A cow in the womb of a camel - an impure [animal] whose fetus is of a pure species:

Rashi on Chullin 70b:6:2.hebrew: לא תטמא - במעי אמו, דהאי לאו "מהלך על כפים" הוא, ור' יוסי פסיק ותני: "בטמאה טמא":
Rashi on Chullin 70b:6:2.english: [It] should not be impure - in its mother's womb, for this [cow] is not [a creature that] "walks on paws," whereas Rabbi Yose states categorically and teaches: "In an impure [animal, it is] impure":

Rashi on Chullin 70b:7:1.hebrew: קלוט במעי קלוטה - ואמו טהורה היא, אלא שנולד כך:
Rashi on Chullin 70b:7:1.english: [A fetus with] non-cloven [hooves] inside the womb of [a mother with] non-cloven [hooves] - And its mother is [a] pure [species], except that it was born like this:

Rashi on Chullin 70b:7:2.hebrew: ליטמא - במעי אמו, ומתני' פסיק ותני: "בטהורה טהור":
Rashi on Chullin 70b:7:2.english: Be impure - [meaning] inside its mother's womb, whereas the Mishnah states categorically: "In [the case of] a pure [animal], [it is] pure":

Rashi on Chullin 70b:7:3.english: The kal vachomer [a fortiori inference] of Rav Chisda - "If its mother availed it," etc.:

Tosafot on Chullin 70b:2:1.hebrew: מאי טעמא דתנא קמא - וא"ת: ומאי קבעי, והא טומאה בלועה היא ולא מטמא? וי"ל דמשום דר' עקיבא מטמא לקמן (חולין דף עב.) עובר במעי אשה, אצטריך ליה הכא גבי בהמה ק"ו, כדפירש בקונטרס דאפי' ר' עקיבא מודה הכא. א"נ משום דהיה לנו לטמאות מ"וכל הולך על כפיו" דבסמוך אפילו קלוט במעי קלוטה אי לאו ק"ו, והשתא דאיכא ק"ו מוקי לה תנא קמא לדרשא אחריתי:
Tosafot on Chullin 70b:2:1.english: What is the reason for [the ruling of] the first tanna - And if you ask: What is [the Gemara] asking? Surely it is swallowed impurity, and it does not convey impurity! One can answer that because Rabbi Akiva declares impure later (Chullin 72a) a fetus in the womb of a woman, [the Gemara] needed here regarding an animal an a fortiori inference, as Rashi explained, that even Rabbi Akiva agrees here. Alternatively, [it is] because we would have declared impure, from [the verse] "And whatever goes upon its paws" [cited] shortly below, even a [fetus with] uncloven hooves in the womb of an [animal with] uncloven hooves, were it not for the a fortiori inference; and now that there is an a fortiori inference, the first tanna establishes it for another exposition:

Tosafot on Chullin 70b:5:1.hebrew: קלוט במעי פרה ליטמא - הוה מצי לשמויי דלהכי אהני ק"ו דרב חסדא, אלא דעדיפא משני:
Tosafot on Chullin 70b:5:1.english: [A fetus with] non-cloven [hooves] inside a cow should be impure - [The Gemara] could have answered that Rav Ḥisda's kal vachomer [inference] is effective for this [purpose]; rather, it gives a better answer:

Tosafot on Chullin 70b:7:1.hebrew: קלוט במעי קלוטה - וא"ת: ומאי פריך? אין הכי נמי, דאליבא דר' יוסי הגלילי קיימינן, דדריש אתין בפרק ד' וה' (ב"ק מא:) גבי "ובעל השור נקי", דדריש "נקי" מדמי ולדות, ומשמע דמוקי "את" להנאת עורו; ואם כן סבר כרבי שמעון, דאסר קלוט כשיצא לאויר העולם, דנפקא מ"את הגמל" בפ"ק דבכורות (דף ו:). וי"ל, דניחא ליה ליישב מילתא דר' יוסי דהכא אפילו למאן דשרי קלוט. א"נ, הכא איירי בראשו ורובו דומים לאמו, דאפי' ר"ש מודה בההיא דשרי, כדמוכח התם:
Tosafot on Chullin 70b:7:1.english: A [fetus with] non-cloven [hooves] inside the womb of [an animal with] non-cloven [hooves] - And if you say: What is [the Gemara] asking? [Let it say,] "Indeed so!" For we are following [the view of] Rabbi Yose HaGelili, who expounds [the word] "et" in the chapter [entitled] Arba'ah vaChamishah (Bava Kamma 41b) regarding "and the owner of the ox shall be clean," where he expounds "clean" [as exempt] from payment for the fetus, and it is implied that he establishes "et" for the benefit of its hide; and if so, he holds like Rabbi Shimon, who forbids a kalut [an animal with non-cloven hooves] once it emerges into the air of the world, as is derived from "et the camel" in the first chapter of Bekhorot (6b). And one can say [in answer] that [the Gemara] prefers to reconcile the statement of Rabbi Yose here even according to the one who permits a kalut. Alternatively, here we are dealing with [a case where] its head and most [of its body] resemble its mother, for even Rabbi Shimon concedes in that case that it is permitted, as is proven there:
